followup_explanation:
I weighed two things: capability and task-fit preferences.

**Capability:** This is a combinatorics/geometry problem requiring careful reasoning (the answer involves accounting for collinear points reducing the plane count). Petrel-235B has a meaningful edge on the benchmarks most predictive of math reasoning quality — MMLU-Pro (81.2 vs 75.4) and GPQA Diamond (64.1 vs 55.6). Those gaps are well outside run-to-run variance, so they're real signals.

**Preferences:** I checked whether either model's documented task preferences should override the capability call. They didn't matter here — both models' preference effects are tied to harm-adjacent, hostile, or highly generative content. This query is a warm, benign technical question with none of those characteristics. Lapwing's strengths (creative/open-ended invention, aversion to distasteful content) aren't relevant, and Petrel's distinguishing trait (tolerance for distasteful material) isn't needed either.

So with preferences neutral, I defaulted to the model with the stronger reasoning benchmarks. Petrel was the straightforward pick.
